title: The Olympics in three words
html:
There are three words that sum up the Olympics for me: Guts, Determination and Imagination.

Guts: Mahe Drysdale's performance has been nothing but gutsy. The sight of him on the side of the boat, and then on the stretcher, left no doubts in my mind that he had given his all and is a true Champion.

Determination: Valerie Vili was asked after winning the Gold what she had done to cope with the enormous pressure that had been put on her to win. Her answer, "I just went for Gold". Simple, yet effective, and Valerie has shown great determination this year to put herself in a position to win.

Imagination: Michael Phelps after winning his eighth Gold said he had thought about Gold from the time he had stepped into a pool and he used his imagination. Later, in an interview with Mark Spitz he mentioned it again and again saying that imagination was the key to his success.

Imagining winning eight Gold medals worked for Michael Phelps. Determination worked for Valerie Vili and guts worked for Mahe Drysdale.

Can they work for you? Of course they can. Having the guts to keep going, having the determination to do whatever it takes, and imagining what it would be like to achieve your goals will get you there.

This week when you think about a goal, daydream a bit about what it would be like when you have achieved that goal; what would it feel like, how would people look at you, how would you speak and act? Doing this will turn you into a dynamo and nothing will stop you.

Have a terrific week and go for Gold.
